title: Reading Input Line by Line
story: while read is the classic way to process lines from a file or a pipe, one at a time.
goal: Read lines from standard input and print each one with its line number, like 1: first line.
hints: Start a counter, then loop with while read -r line.
Inside the loop add one to the counter and echo it.

n=0
while read -r line; do
  n=$((n + 1))
  echo "$n: $line"
done
socratic: Where does read take its input from?
explain: In one sentence: what did you learn from “Reading Input Line by Line”?
solution:
n=0
while read -r line; do
  n=$((n + 1))
  echo "$n: $line"
done
alt:
i=1
while IFS= read -r l; do
  printf '%d: %s\n' "$i" "$l"
  ((i++))
done
